newsitem.title: USA: U.S. calls Israel's settlements move troubling.
newsitem.headline: U.S. calls Israel's settlements move troubling.

text.p: The United States described as "troubling" Israel's decision Friday to grant financial benefits to Jewish settlers in the West Bank and suggested it was aimed at pre-empting Middle East peace talks.

The Israeli move, which could lead more Jews to settle in the occupied area, was a strong sign of defiance by right-wing Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to world opposition to his plans to tighten Israel's hold on captured Arab land.

"We've seen the statement and frankly it's troubling," State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns said. "As I said before many times, settlement activity is unhelpful and...clearly complicates the peace process."

But in remarks going beyond standard U.S. phraseology, Burns added: "There's no doubt that when either side says or does things that are seen to pre-empt the outcome of a negotiation, it makes it that much more difficult to achieve progress in those negotiations."

Israel and the Palestinians are supposed to start talks this year which would deal with the "final status" of Palestinian self-rule areas in the West Bank and Gaza foreseen under the Oslo peace accords.

Palestinians argue that settlements -- which were frozen by the previous Labour government but are now being expanded by Netanyahu -- are an attempt to create "facts on the ground" to prevent them from taking control of the area.

The start of the final status talks has been delayed by the inability of the sides so far to agree on a pull-back of Israeli troops from the West Bank town of Hebron, the last of seven towns where they are due to redeploy under Oslo.

The deadlock over Hebron and the renewed Israeli settlement activity has caused increasing frustration in Washington, reflected in a small but noticeable toughening in the language of U.S. statements on the issue.

The Israeli cabinet's decision Friday will reinstate benefits for West Bank settlers, such as lower taxes, that are already given to residents of development towns inside Israel, Israelis in Gaza and those in the occupied Golan Heights.
The Palestinian Information Ministry termed Israel's move "a direct call for violence and a declaration of war on the Palestinian people and its National Authority".
